Khmelnytskyy Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the older of two documented cemeteries serving Khmelnytskyi, a city with a Jewish presence from 1629 that survived the Khmelnytsky massacres of 1648–49 and grew to a reported 11,411 people by 1897 — though the source's own cited percentage figure for that year is not credible and is omitted here. A pogrom by Petliura's forces killed 1,600 Jews in February 1919. During WWII, two ghettos held over 10,000 prisoners; October 1942 saw 5,300 executed, followed by more than 7,000 on November 30, and a final 2,000 during the camp's liquidation. Three memorials were erected in the city after the war.
